summary: ASTRA Twin is a prototype that builds a personal digital twin of each astronaut's health. It compares each astronaut to their own baseline instead of generic limits, so slow drifts in heart rate, sleep, mood and other signals can be noticed earlier. It suggests likely causes, and writes delay-aware action guidance and reports for the flight surgeon. It uses simulated data.https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1fxmBPK9N-NMz6BnRBF_7xzFKwFkvTSmR/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=114333236277418179903&rtpof=true&sd=true
details:
WHAT IT DOES

ASTRA Twin is a decision-support prototype (a Google Colab notebook) for monitoring astronaut health on long missions. It simulates a 30-day mission for a 4-person crew (all data is simulated) with 8 indicators: resting heart rate, HRV, systolic blood pressure, body temperature, blood glucose, sleep, mood and reaction time.

For each astronaut, the first 7 days set a personal baseline. A Kalman filter smooths the data and tracks slow drift from that baseline. Changes are grouped into four body systems (cardiovascular, sleep and cognition, immune and metabolic, behavioural) and rated Green, Yellow, Orange or Red, with a 0-100 readiness score. An Isolation Forest model adds an anomaly score that catches unusual combinations of signals.

The notebook also includes: a simple correlation-based check that suggests a likely cause (radiation, isolation drift or low exercise); an illustrative what-if model for exercise vs bone density and aerobic fitness; a rule-based decision guide that depends on Earth communication delay; an automatically generated SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) report; a crew readiness heatmap; and a signal-processing demo that estimates heart rate from a synthetic video-style signal (rPPG). It also contains code that downloads solar energetic particle events from the NASA DONKI API.

BENEFITS

The idea is to compare each astronaut to their own baseline instead of generic limits, so slow personal drifts can be noticed earlier. Reports and suggested actions are generated automatically to support crews who face communication delays with Earth.

INTENDED IMPACT

A starting point for personalised, delay-aware health monitoring on long missions to the Moon and Mars. It is a decision-support prototype only, not a medical diagnosis tool. The health data is simulated and the what-if model is illustrative, not clinically validated.

TOOLS

Python, Google Colab, NumPy, pandas, matplotlib, scikit-learn (Isolation Forest), ipywidgets and the Requests library. No special hardware is needed.

CREATIVITY

It combines a per-astronaut baseline, cause suggestions, a what-if simulator, delay-aware decision guidance and automatic reports in one notebook.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

Individual differences between astronauts, Earth communication delay, space radiation, isolation and reduced exercise as mission stressors, and clear labelling of simulated data and prototype limits.
